old: for man cannot live without God in the world
new: for man cannot live without the favor of heaven
reason: The rest of the Book consistently speaks of 'the gods,' 'heaven,' and 'the immortals' (polytheistic framing). This is the only spot with singular, capitalized 'God,' which reads as a monotheistic slip and could genuinely confuse a listener about which world/religion the story is set in.

old: to whom Agamemnon had given strict orders on setting out for Troy that he was to keep guard over his wife
new: to whom Agamemnon, on setting out for Troy, had given strict orders to keep guard over Clytemnestra
reason: Both pronouns are ambiguous on first hearing: 'he' (the bard, who is to keep guard) and 'his wife' (Agamemnon's wife, not the bard's) sit right next to each other, inviting the momentary misreading that the bard is guarding his own wife.

old: the Trito-born, who showed such favor to your brave father among the Argives
new: who showed such favor to your brave father among the Argives
reason: 'The Trito-born' is an obscure epithet for Athena that isn't explained anywhere in the text; a first-time listener has no way to connect it to the goddess already named a clause earlier ('Zeus's formidable daughter') and it adds nothing they can use.
